subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a fixed stable package for the `2026.6.11` reply-session package regression now, or keep this open until the next normal stable release replaces npm `latest`?
rationale: Current main has source-side fixes, but npm stable latest still points to the affected artifact; choosing a hotfix/backport, normal release, or user guidance path is a release-ownership decision automation cannot safely make.

options.title: Publish fixed stable package
options.body: Build from a selected fixed source commit, verify the npm tarball contains the reentrant writer and reply-init identity changes, publish it as stable, and close this issue with release proof.

options.title: Wait for next stable
options.body: Keep this issue open as a release blocker and clearly steer users away from `2026.6.11` until the next stable release replaces npm `latest`.

options.title: Close as main-only fixed
options.body: Treat current main as sufficient and close now, accepting that ordinary stable npm installs remain affected until a later release.

recommendation.title: Publish fixed stable package
recommendation.body: Build from a selected fixed source commit, verify the npm tarball contains the reentrant writer and reply-init identity changes, publish it as stable, and close this issue with release proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is release/package handling, and this handle is tied to the relevant `v2026.6.11` release commits.
